first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down QoQ, indicating friction in the conversion funnel. Memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB) and memory_86 (shortening onboarding for adoption lift) directly address both metrics. Verifying these will confirm whether the durable uplift persists and whether similar field reduction or streamlining approaches remain effective. This addresses root cause (friction) rather than symptom (price sensitivity). Referral incentives and enterprise sales assist are lower urgency given current activation decline. Promotional pricing addresses competitor threat but risks margin degradation without solving the underlying activation problem. A standard experiment on simplified onboarding targets the primary symptom pair and leverages proven mechanisms while preserving the option to deploy pricing or enterprise tactics if activation doesn't recover.

final.rationale: Verified records show signup simplification lifted SMB activation +9% and qualified revenue +4% with only -1% retention risk, while shortened onboarding improved completion +13% and retention +3%. Both mechanisms are proven and directly address the current QoQ declines in activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%). The verified retention gains (esp. from exp_86) mitigate short-term pressure and protect long-term qualified revenue. This approach targets root cause (friction) rather than treating symptoms. Competitor pricing pressure is real but promotional pricing would likely erode margins without solving activation decay. Enterprise sales assist is premature given the self-serve funnel is underperforming. A standard experiment combining simplified signup and streamlined onboarding flows on SMB cohorts leverages dual proven levers, preserves uncertainty on interaction effects, and positions follow-up pricing or sales-assist plays if activation remains weak.
